transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thanks so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm in the right place for this. I guess I'm here because I've been having a little bit of trouble with... well, with eating lately. It's probably nothing major, but I just wanted to be safe. 

I work late shifts at an entertainment center, and when I get off, I usually stop to grab some food. Which I think is pretty normal, right? But then I get home and I just... I kind of keep going. Like, I'll finish a full takeout meal, and then I'll have some chips, or sweets... really just whatever is in the apartment. And afterward, I'm just kind of shocked by how much I actually ate. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
After you eat a large amount of food, do you ever make yourself vomit, use laxatives, or do anything else to try to compensate for what you've eaten?

Oh, um... well... I try not to do anything too extreme, you know? I really do try to take good care of myself. But... I guess, sometimes... if I really overdo it with the takeout or all those snacks after my shift... I might, um... well, I sometimes go to the bathroom and just... make myself throw up. 

It's not every single time, I promise. Just when I feel like I ate way too much and I'm worried it's just going to sit in me and turn into weight. I just don't want to let myself go, you know? I hope that doesn't sound too awful... is that something you see a lot?
How often do you find yourself making yourself vomit after eating, and how do you feel about doing it?

Well, um... I guess since I moved into my new apartment and things kind of settled into a routine, it's been happening a bit more. I'd say... maybe most weeks, I have at least one of those late nights where I just eat way past what I meant to. 

And then, yeah, I'll try to make up for it. Sometimes by throwing up, like I mentioned... or maybe I'll just skip breakfast the next day, or force myself to go on a really long run to burn it off. 

As for how I feel about it... I mean, I don't love doing it. It's not ideal, I know that. But in the moment, it just feels like the only way to fix the mistake, you know? I just want to keep things balanced. I'm really trying my best to stay healthy... I hope you understand. Does that make sense, doctor?
Can you tell me how many times in the last week you made yourself vomit or used other behaviors to compensate for eating?

Um, let's see... the last week. I mean, it really wasn't too bad this past week, I don't think. I always try to be really careful. 

If I had to guess, maybe... just once or twice? Like I said, it's really just when things get a little out of hand after work, and I just want to make sure I don't let myself go. I didn't do anything crazy, I promise. Just trying to keep everything under control. 

Is that... I mean, is that a lot? I hope that doesn't sound too terrible. I'm really trying to do the right thing here.

Can you tell me how many times in the past week you've had episodes where you felt you were eating a large amount of food in a short period of time and felt like you couldn't stop, even if you weren't doing anything to compensate afterward?

Um, well... like I think I mentioned a little bit ago, ever since the apartment move settled into a routine, it's usually just... maybe once a week. Most weeks I have at least one of those late-night episodes where I just eat way past what I meant to, and I feel like I just can't stop. And then, you know, that's when I try to make up for it by throwing up, or skipping breakfast, or forcing myself to do a really long run. 

So for this past week specifically... it was really just that one time. I promise I didn't let it happen more than that. I'm really trying to keep a handle on it. Does that... does that sound like I'm doing okay? I just don't want you to think I'm completely out of control.
When you're eating a large amount of food during these episodes, do you feel like you have no control over your eating, like you can't stop even if you want to?

Um, yeah, I guess... I guess that's exactly how it feels. It's kind of embarrassing to admit, to be honest. I mean, I'm a grown man, I should be able to just... stop eating, right? But... 

Once I start on those nights, it's almost like... like I'm watching myself from the outside. I'll be standing there in the kitchen, telling myself, you know, "Just put the food away, you've had enough," but my hands just keep opening containers and wrappers until... until everything is just gone. 

It's not that I want to be doing it, I really don't. It just sort of takes over for a little bit. But like I said, it's only once a week, so it's not like an every night kind of thing. I'm really trying to get better at catching myself before it gets to that point. I hope you don't think less of me for it... I know it sounds a bit weak, doesn't it?
Do these episodes and the things you do afterward cause you a lot of distress, or interfere with your daily life in any way?

Um, well... I wouldn't say a *lot* of distress. I really try not to let it get in the way of the important things, you know? Like, I'm still showing up for work every single day and doing a good job, I promise. 

But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest... it does interfere a little bit. I've started kind of dodging those after-shift meals with my coworkers. It's just easier to avoid them so I don't slip up or put myself in a bad spot. And... well, my mornings can get a bit complicated. Instead of just resting before my next shift or getting my errands out of the way, I sort of have to plan my whole morning around... you know, undoing the night before. Making sure I get that run in or whatever I need to do to fix it. 

But I'm still holding down my job and paying my bills! It's mostly just a little bit of a scheduling thing, really. That doesn't sound too awful, right? I'm really trying my best to keep it from affecting my life too much. I hope you can see I'm trying.
Can you tell me if there have been times when you've eaten a lot of food in a short period of time and felt like you couldn't stop yourself, even if you didn't try to compensate for it afterward?

Um, well... I don't think so? I mean, like I said, when it happens, I always try to fix it right away. I don't really just... let it sit there. 

If I mess up and eat too much, I always make sure I do something about it, whether that's the running or, um, the other things. I wouldn't just eat like that and then do nothing. That would be really irresponsible, wouldn't it? I always try to make it right. So, no, I don't think I've ever just had the eating part without the... the fixing part. Does that make sense? I hope that's the right answer.
Can you think of a time when you felt you couldn’t stop yourself from eating, even if you didn’t do anything to compensate for it afterward?

Oh, um, I'm sorry, did I not explain that right just a second ago? My apologies, I might not have been very clear. But, um, no... I really can't think of a time like that. 

Like I was just saying, I would never just... eat all that food and not try to fix it. That would feel really out of control, and I'm really trying hard to keep things manageable, you know? So I always make sure to go for that run or... do whatever I need to do to balance it out. I promise I don't just let myself go and do nothing about it. 

Does that answer what you're looking for? I'm sorry if I misunderstood the question the first time, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Even if you later tried to compensate, can you recall any specific times when, while eating, you felt completely unable to stop yourself even if you wanted to?

Um, yeah... I guess, if I'm being completely honest, there is that feeling. I don't want you to think I'm totally out of control, because I do fix it after, like I said! But... during the actual eating part... 

It's sort of like... once I start on those nights, it's almost like I'm watching myself from the outside? Like I'm in my head telling myself to just put the food away, that I don't need it, but... my hands just keep opening containers anyway. And I just keep going until everything is gone. 

It sounds really bad when I say it out loud, doesn't it? I'm sorry, I know it's not a good thing. I really do try to stop, I just... in that specific moment, it feels really hard to. But that's why I always make sure to run or do whatever I have to do the next morning, to make up for it. I'm trying to be better about it, I promise. Is that... is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
How often have you used behaviors like making yourself vomit, using laxatives, or doing excessive exercise to try to undo the effects of overeating in the past month?

Um, well... I really don't want it to sound like I'm doing this all the time, because I'm not. But, um, since the apartment move kind of settled down and I got into a routine... I guess most weeks there's at least one night where I end up eating way more than I meant to. 

And then, you know, because I don't want to just leave it like that—because that wouldn't be good—I try to make up for it. So I might... make myself sick, or just skip breakfast the next day, or force myself to go on a really long run. Just to balance it out, you know? It's usually just once a week, maybe. I hope that doesn't sound too awful. I really am trying to keep it under control. Is that... does that help answer your question?
